doc.title: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor Interview, 1961-05-23
doc.interviewee: Ralph Emerson Brown and Jasper Taylor

title: Sidney Bechet and the soprano saxophone, tuning and tone
summary: They discuss Bechet's clarinet and soprano playing, his trip with Will Marion Cook, Brown's dislike of his soprano tone and intonation, and why audiences like slightly off-pitch sounds.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: In a sense I think that those clarinet players, Barney and Noon especially, were part of a family. In other words they were not especially creators even though they had great originality and you identify them immediately. They're of a family, maybe comes back from Teal. Teal and Bache.

Teal was probably the greatest of the Teal. He laid out in the style. Then Bache came along before he took up that old soprano sax. I never could see why Bache took that dog on soprano sax. Yet he made a whole lot of money with it. Well see people don't, they're lame like that's paying the bills, they don't know anything about what's going on.

Well actually it may have been the same sense of novelty that you noticed when you started off with an alto. It was a novel thing. Well it caught on to where it became a conventional instrument. Maybe the soprano could have become a conventional instrument instead of a bastard instrument but it has remained.

It was said, yeah but he played, people went for it. He said, see people like, people let's go for something that's offside. Yeah. But Bache, Clarnett, well that guy was a wonderful, wonderful, wonderful. Now he went overseas with a fellow named Will Mann Cook and Bache, never was a good reader. But Will Mann Cook was one of those particular guys.
He was on soprano by the time he went with Cook wasn't he? I think probably he was.

I thought he went with a listener on his clarinet but I thought, I'm not sure. But he set a good style for clarinet oh years ago. A good style for clarinet. And I don't know, maybe he saw so many clarinet players come along and he said, I'll take this soprano. And he took it and made God rich of it. But I had a lot of soprano saxophone. I just don't like to tell them what they had. Well of course I'm me about what does me, what I like or dislike. But Bache did some with it all right. But Charlotte Bonnet and a few others played in tune. Charlotte Bonnet and a few others played. Boyan Fields used to play with the . Those two folks played in tune.
You've heard Johnny Hodges play soprano.
Oh yes, Johnny does. He's old, he's fast, he's green light on soprano. Those three to me played in tune. But to me, Bache did ever play in tune. Maybe that's what took the people. You see them?

There's a lot of people, there's a lot of people who go for something that's just a little bit under what it should be. And a lot of these guys, some of these guys, we play in chord tones in certain things. But it seems like it's something that hits people. Something that's just a little bit offside.
Maybe get more emotional impact. I guess so, I guess so. Do you think Bache was mainly flat?

Well, it just seemed like it never seemed to be in tune to me. To me, he just never, he played with us out on Long Island, come out a couple of times, and played with us, just for fun of it. Of course, one time, I was playing in Long Island, Jeff Bache was, wasn't doing so good, he'd open up a place, a gambling place, and he'd lost all his money. He'd had money once, but he was broke at that time. And I don't know, I'd heard the guy play clarinet before, and just to me, maybe I was prejudiced. I'd heard him play this fine clarinet, and that old, that old, uh.
Well, he didn't play the clarinet out of tune as he did the soprano. Or you didn't notice it? No. I didn't know it. To me, he's just a natural kind of player. Just natural.

But the old soprano, I just never did it. Maybe it wasn't out of tune, but I just didn't like the old tone of it. To me, it wasn't a good tone. But what I call good tone, lots of other people, they like something that's a little, they call it a little weird or something. Just a little kind of off color. I guess there's something to it, because now, you take Glenn Miller and his fine arrangements, he used to carry a dissonant interval sometimes. It's all fine. But of course, those guys are all in tune. They had to be in tune to play that and sell those records. But he used to really carry, purposefully carry a dissonant interval in quite a bit of his arrangements. But he'd have these other ones down so low, and the other ones on top, but you could tell there's something odd about it. And people, it was still people's ease. I guess maybe those things are a little bit offside, I guess, maybe get to some people. I guess, you and nation are strange things. A lot of people don't want to think it's right. So I guess that's what you would do.
